question: Can one autoregressive model trained to classify the next text token and regress the next visual embedding, on image-text, interleaved document and interleaved video data, serve as a generalist interface for both image-to-text and text-to-image tasks?
hypothesis: Supervising the vision side with a next-embedding regression loss, and adding video as a source of interleaved data, improves multimodal capacity over LMMs that only predict text.
contributions: Emu: a 14B multimodal model trained end-to-end with one objective, classifying the next text token or regressing the next visual embedding.
A Causal Transformer that turns 2D EVA-CLIP features into N 1D causal embeddings per image.
YT-Storyboard-1B: interleaved video-text data built from YouTube storyboard thumbnails and subtitles.
Zero-shot and few-shot results on captioning, image and video QA and text-to-image generation, plus an instruction-tuned assistant (Emu-I).

method.summary: EVA-CLIP encodes images, a 12-block Causal Transformer compresses them to N visual embeddings, and these are interleaved with text tokens in a LLaMA-13B-initialised LLM trained with cross-entropy on text and l2 regression on visual embeddings. After pretraining, a Stable Diffusion v1.5 U-Net is fine-tuned to decode the LLM's regressed embeddings into images; a LoRA instruction-tuned variant (Emu-I) is also built.
method.task: Unified next-element prediction over interleaved image/video/text sequences; image captioning, VQA, video QA, text-to-image

models.name: Emu
models.architecture: EVA-01-CLIP encoder + 12-block Causal Transformer + decoder-only LLaMA + Stable Diffusion decoder
models.init_from: EVA-01-CLIP 1B (encoder), LLaMA-13B (LLM), Stable Diffusion v1.5 (decoder), Causal Transformer random init

models.name: Emu-I
models.architecture: Emu with LoRA on self-attention of the LLM

other.LoRA: rank 16, alpha 16, on all linear projections of self-attention; no adaptation on vision encoder

models.name: Flamingo-9B / Flamingo-80B, Kosmos-1, MetaLM, PaLI-X-55B, GILL, SDv1.5, Imagen, Parti, DALL-E 2, GLIDE, Make-A-Scene, CM3Leon, AnyMAL-13B, MM-Vet comparison models

training.objective: Next-element prediction: cross-entropy on discrete text tokens (language modeling head), l2 regression on continuous visual embeddings (separate regression head)
training.lr: peak 4e-5 vision encoder, 3e-5 LLM, 1e-4 Causal Transformer (pretraining); decoder warm up to 1e-4 over first 5k, then 5e-5 at 10k and 1e-5 at 14k; instruction tuning 1e-5
training.lr_schedule: cosine decay (pretraining); instruction tuning cosine to zero
training.batch_size: pretraining per dataset 128, 128, 64, 16, 16 (Table 5); text says 128 image-text pairs, 64 interleaved image-text, 16 video-text and interleaved video-text; decoder 50 x 4 x 8; instruction tuning 128
training.epochs: instruction tuning 3 epochs for ShareGPT, Alpaca, LLaVA; 60K samples for video instruction data
training.tokens: around 82M samples (150B tokens in total) pretraining
training.seq_len: MMC4 subsequences L=1024 or L=512; otherwise null
training.regularisation: Image embedding condition randomly dropped 10% of the time in decoder training for classifier-free guidance
training.wall_clock: about 2 days pretraining; about 16 hours instruction tuning

other.decoder frozen parts: Visual Encoder, LLM and VAE frozen; only U-Net updated
other.frames: 8 frames randomly sampled per video in pretraining; images randomly placed before or after their sentence

inference.decoding: Image generation: PNDM scheduler, 50 steps, classifier-free guidance. Text decoding settings not stated.
inference.samples: FID on 30k random MS-COCO val prompts; MM-Vet mean and std over 5 evaluation runs
inference.prompting: Zero-shot with task templates (Table 10), multimodal chain-of-thought (generate caption, then answer); * rows use two text-only task examples chosen by RICES; few-shot k=2,4,8 via RICES
inference.retrieval: RICES: 5000 random training samples per dataset, EVA-CLIP features, highest cosine similarity; video uses mean of frame features; 8 frames for query video, 2 frames for support video examples

other.VizWiz: model first asked 'is the answer known?' (yes/no); 'no' returns 'unanswerable'
other.OKVQA: VQAv2 evaluation code with Porter stemming

metrics.name: VQA accuracy
metrics.definition: VQAv2 test-dev, OKVQA val, VizWiz test-dev

metrics.name: MM-Vet capability scores
metrics.definition: Rec, OCR, Know, Gen, Spat, Math, Total; mean and std of 5 runs

eval.protocol: Zero-shot (with multimodal CoT) and few-shot k=2,4,8; single runs except MM-Vet (5 runs); no significance tests; some results from official evaluation websites

results.claim: Emu has a zero-shot COCO caption CIDEr of 112.4, above the other LMMs in Table 1.
results.setup: Pretrained 14B Emu, zero-shot, with multimodal chain-of-thought prompting (caption first, then answer); COCO caption test
results.quote: Emu achieves impressive zero-shot CIDEr score (Vedantam et al., 2015) of 112.4

results.claim: Emu's zero-shot COCO FID is worse than SDv1.5 but better than GILL.
results.setup: Zero-shot, 30k random MS-COCO val prompts, PNDM scheduler 50 steps, classifier-free guidance scale 5.0 for Emu and 3.0 for SDv1.5 (chosen as best for each)
results.note: Table 11 also lists CM3Leon at 10.82 FID, better than Emu, yet the text says Emu is state-of-the-art on 5 of 6 benchmarks there.

results.claim: The authors attribute the FID gap to SDv1.5 to condition-space mismatch and short decoder training (conjecture, not tested).
results.quote: This is probably because the condition space (image embeddings) of our visual decoder deviates a lot from the condition space (text embeddings) of the diffusion model used as initialization, and our model is trained for a relatively short 15k steps.

results.claim: Instruction-tuned Emu-I beats Flamingo-80B on VQAv2, VizWiz and MSVDQA zero-shot.
results.setup: Zero-shot, Emu-I* (two text-only examples as prompt), 14B. VizWiz 38.3 vs 31.6, MSVDQA 37.0 vs 35.6. Flamingo-80B figures are quoted from Flamingo, not in Table 1.
results.quote: Emu-I can outperform much larger-scale Flamingo-80B model in several tasks such as VQAv2 (62.0% vs. 56.3%), VizWiz (38.3% vs. 31.6%), and MSVDQA (37.0% vs. 35.6%).
results.note: Without the * prompt Emu-I scores lower on VizWiz (32.2) than Emu (34.2), and on NExTQA (5.8 vs 19.6).

results.claim: Emu 4-shot beats Flamingo-9B on VQAv2 and VizWiz.
results.setup: Pretrained Emu, 4 in-context examples selected by RICES. VizWiz 41.3 vs 34.9.
results.quote: Emu achieves a VQAv2 accuracy of 58.4% and VizWiz 41.3% under the 4-shot setting, surpassing Flamingo-9B by +2.1% and +6.4%, respectively.
4-shot 21.8% v.s. Flamingo’s 18.2% on the MSRVTTQA benchmark

results.claim: Emu on VizWiz (zero-shot, text-only-example row) beats Kosmos-1 and Flamingo-9B.
results.quote: Notably, Emu achieves an accuracy of 34.4% on the complex VizWiz VQA dataset, versus Kosmos-1’s 29.2% and Flamingo-9B’s 28.8%.
results.note: 34.4 is the Emu * row; plain Emu is 34.2.

results.claim: Emu-I-14B total MM-Vet score is 36.3, above LLaVA-65B (35.5) and DreamLLM-7B (35.9).
results.setup: Zero-shot, MM-Vet, mean of 5 evaluation runs
results.note: Emu-I is below LLaVA-65B on OCR (19.2 vs 28.2), Spat and Math (3.8 vs 15.0).

results.claim: Adding YT-Storyboard-1B improves the 7B ablation modestly on COCO CIDEr and MSVDQA, but lowers OKVQA k=0*.
results.setup: Emu-7B (EVA-CLIP-Large + LLaMA-7B), 7.2k steps on pairs plus 2.4k extra on YT-Storyboard-1B, single run. MSVDQA k=4 34.9 vs 31.1; OKVQA k=0* 42.3 vs 43.9.
results.table: Table 6, row Emu-7B w/ YT-Storyboard-1B, column COCO k=0

results.quote: we can observe a positive correlation between the number of shots k (k = 0, 2, 4, 8) and the performance of Emu
results.note: Claimed for k=0 too, but Table 3 has no k=0 column.

results.claim: Against CM3Leon (discrete image tokens), Emu scores far higher on COCO captioning.
results.setup: Zero-shot, Table 11; CM3Leon figures copied from that work (evaluation conditions not described). CM3Leon FID 10.82 is better than Emu 11.66.
results.quote: We can find that CM3Leon performs much worse than Emu on image-to-text tasks.

results.claim: Pretraining cost: 128 A100-80G, 10k steps, about 2 days.
results.quote: We train the model on 128 NVIDIA 80G-A100 GPUs for 10k steps with around 82M samples (150B tokens in total), and the pretraining takes approximately 2 days.

results.claim: Storyboard thumbnails instead of raw video cut data storage 20-fold and avoid video decoding.
results.setup: YT-Storyboard-1B versus raw video; no measurement shown
results.quote: this approach leads to a substantial 20-fold reduction in data storage costs

results.claim: Instruction tuning takes about 16 hours on 16 A100-80G.
results.quote: The overall instruction tuning stage takes around 16 hours with 16 A100-80G GPUs.

limits: Authors concede hallucination, slow autoregressive inference, no knowledge updates after pretraining, non-factual output, and English-dominated data.
No ablation of regression versus discrete tokens or of the Causal Transformer; the only ablation is YT-Storyboard-1B on a 7B variant, single run.
Image generation is evaluated only by FID on COCO plus qualitative figures; no human evaluation or CLIP-score.
Emu's FID is worse than SDv1.5; the cause offered (condition-space mismatch, short training) is untested.

Evaluation uses multimodal CoT captioning and task templates tuned per benchmark; * rows use text-only examples, so numbers depend on prompt format. Flamingo-80B and other baseline figures are copied, not rerun.
Paper says model is preliminary, research only; ethics section flags inherited bias and privacy risk.

terms.definition: transforms 2D spatial visual signals to 1D causal sequences in a latent space; accepts N randomly initialised embeddings and outputs N embeddings conditioned on EVA-CLIP features via cross-attention
interleaved video-text data from YouTube storyboard thumbnails and subtitles ordered by timestamp
Retrieval In-Context Example Selection: choose in-context examples by highest cosine similarity of EVA-CLIP features

lineage.note: Compared throughout; RICES and text-only-example prompting follow it
Initialises the visual decoder; v1.5 is a baseline
Discretises images, whereas Emu uses continuous features

figures.caption: Emu unifies the modeling of different modalities in an auto-regressive manner. Visual signals are first encoded into embeddings, and together with text tokens form an interleaved sequence. The training objective is to either classify the next text token or regress the next visual embedding.
figures.why: Shows the whole pipeline: classification head for text, regression head for visual embeddings, decoder at inference.

figures.caption: Interleaved video-text data. The combination of storyboard thumbnails and subtitles captions creates a natural interleaved sequence of video and text that is ordered by the timestamps.
Zero-shot text-to-image results on MS-COCO validation set. 30k samples are randomly sampled for evaluation.
figures.why: The FID comparison against SDv1.5, GILL and others.
